# dsh-penpot-plugin

Penpot for DeepSeek Harness: list, search,
inspect and export design files from a DSH agent over Pen
pot's local HTTP API.

`0.2` is deliberately read + export. Writing designs needs Penpot's
`update-file` change format; the

design questions are in
docs/DESIGN.md.

There is no MCP backend. The setup runs a local Penpot instance and talks to it
over `/api/rpc/comma

nd/*` with an access token; a second transport added a
read-only path that could not export, so it w
as removed in 0.2.0.

`PENPOT_ACCESS_TOKEN` into the runtime e

nvironment, installs the pinned plugin
and mounts a managed `dsh-penpot` row. Nothing below is neede

and mounts a managed `dsh-penpot` row. Nothing below is needed.
### Configure in the UI

On DSH `0.2.1-rc.5` or newer, open **Plugins** → **dsh-penpot-plugin** and press
**Configure** on th
e `dsh-penpot` row. Set:

- **API URL** — the Penpot origin, for example `http://192.168.2.98:8090`
(no `/api/rpc` suffix; `ht

tps://…:8443` works when the CA is trusted).
- **Access token** — create it in Penpot → Settings → A

works when the CA is trusted).
- **Access token** — create it in Penpot → Settings → Access tokens.

**Save** writes the row's config into the profile's user layer; the plugin
recomposes with it. The m

anaged setup's row still falls back to
`PENPOT_API_URL`/`PENPOT_ACCESS_TOKEN` in the runtime environ

ment, and the UI
values override them. Without the UI (older DSH or a headless profile), use the
env
ironment or the `cordis.patch.yml` row as described below.
### Standalone (any DSH runtime)
See docs/STANDALONE.md for the complete walkthrough.

The plugin is a normal DSH bundle: it works in any profile, with or without the
setup. It needs a Pe

npot instance and an access token, nothing else from this
project. It is published to npm as an exac

project. It is published to npm as an exact version:

The registry tarball contains the built `lib/`, so there is no `prepare` build
and no `allowBuilds`
entry. Restart the runtime after adding it.
From the source repository instead, allow the build and pin the tag:

The row reads its credentials from the
environment of the **runtime process** — exporting them in a

shell later does

In the DSH setup that means adding both to `.env` and restarting
`dsh.service`; the design component

does it for you. Ask the agent for
`penpot_status` to verify: it names the endpoint, and a missing

variable is
reported by name.
## Tools
| Tool | What it does |

| `penpot_status` | whether the API is configured, and its endpoint |
| `penpot_teams` | teams the a

ccount can see |
| `penpot_projects` | projects, optionally per team |
| `penpot_files` | files in a

project |
| `penpot_search` | files by name or term |
| `penpot_file` | one file: id, name, pages |

| `penpot_export` | write a `.penpot` file to disk |
| `penpot_import` | upload a `.penpot` file as
a new or replacement file |

Export gives a zip of Penpot JSON: unzip it, read or edit with the normal file
tools, then import it

back with `penpot_import` — no setup CLI and no second
toolchain. A new file needs `projectId`; rep
lacing one needs `fileId`.
## Backend
One backend: Penpot's HTTP RPC.

- `POST /api/rpc/command/<name>` with `Authorization: Token …`, kebab-case
payloads (`get-teams`, `g

et-all-projects`, `get-files`, `search-files`,
`get-file-summary`, `export-binfile`, `import-binfile

`).
- Configuration is `apiUrl` + `token`; both come from the environment in the
setup's managed row

. If either is empty the plugin still loads, and
`penpot_status` says `none` while the other tools e

y the plugin still loads, and
`penpot_status` says `none` while the other tools explain what to set.

## Updating
Plugin versions are independent of DSH and of the setup release.

- **In the setup:** `/system update penpot` in the bot (or `/system update
plugin dsh-penpot-plugin`

) resolves the newest version, opens a rollback trial,
and replaces the bundle through the host's pl

ugin manager.
- **Standalone:** `dsh plugin --profile <name> remove dsh-penpot-plugin`, then
`add` t

he new tag. The plugin manager cannot install over an already-installed
git package, so it is two st

eps; restart the runtime when it reports
`restart-required`.

The `dsh-penpot` row's configuration is preserved across an update; only the
package moves.
## Compatibility

Plugin versions are independent of DSH and of the setup release. Each release
states the DSH range a

nd the Penpot versions it was tested against in
COMPATIBILITY.md. The setup pins an exact npm spec i

n
`plugins.json`; a newer compatible version installed from the bot stays
installed across reboots,

and the GitHub tag of the same release is the
registry-unreachable fallback.
